description: The image is a false-colour satellite or aerial photograph depicting sclerophyllous vegetation in Loutsa, on the Island of Evia, Greece. The central area is dominated by dark reddish-purple vegetation, which represents dense sclerophyllous scrubland. The species identified in the image caption for this type of vegetation include _Asparagus_ sp., _Euphorbia_ sp., _Cistus_ sp., and _Olea europaea_ var. _sylvestris_. This reddish-purple hue in false-colour imagery often indicates vegetation with specific spectral reflectance characteristics common in Mediterranean `maquis`, `garrigue`, or `phrygana` ecosystems. Brighter green areas are visible towards the top-right and along some slopes, suggesting different vegetation types, possibly healthier forests or pastures. Lighter pink/reddish tones represent sparser vegetation or drier soil. Irregular, thin green lines are overlaid on the landscape, likely delineating land cover boundaries, habitat parcels, or other geographical features. A linear reddish-pink feature, potentially a dry riverbed or a track, traverses the lower-right portion of the image. The image credit is N. Kolpatzik.
